newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower, new crop down on hedge sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower, new crop down on hedge sales.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended lower Tuesday, with new crop contracts under hedge pressure and spot contracts down on technical weakness, floor traders said.
"We are technically weak because we made new highs last week and we weren't able to get past them again," said one pit trader.
Some of Tuesday's selling was also said to originate in the options pit, floor traders said.
The market continued to find support from the slow pace of new crop rice planting in major U.S. rice producing states.
In Texas, the rice crop was 12 percent planted.
That figure compares to 69 percent a year ago, and the five-year average of 54 percent, according to the weekly crop report from the Texas State Agricultural Statistics office.
Traders were still awaiting news of a Costa Rican rice tender. Results were expected soon, and some exporters said the business could go to U.S. dealers.
Rice ended 0.05 to 0.08 per cwt lower, with July off eight at $11.60.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 250 lots, down slightly from Monday's actual volume of 295 lots, according to CBOT data.
